answer: On a wind-scoured coast, iron sand piles into dunes, and each agent tends one dune crest. Every dawn the keeper reads the ripple lines the night wind pressed into the sand, sifts one scoop through a hand magnet, and weighs the ferrous grains it pulls out. Both numbers go into a logbook, and a second keeper repeats the sift at dusk and checks them against the dawn entry. A crest with smoothed ripples or a failed weight loses its plot for a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand dunes walked at dawn and a thousand magnets weighed twice a day.
